title: High Throughput Microfluidic Rapid and Low Cost Prototyping Packaging Methods
protocol: Mix PDMS and curing agent with a ratio of 10:1.
Ensure the oven temperature is stabilized at 80 °C.
Clean the Petri dish thoroughly with ethanol.
Clean the surface of the microfluidic access holes where the PDMS interconnector will be placed.
Pour a thin layer (approximately 2 mm) of the PDMS into the Petri dish.
Let the PDMS slightly polymerize in an oven at 80 °C for 12-15 min.
Place the microfluidic chip to which the connection will be made in the oven simultaneously with the PDMS.
Remove the PDMS from the curing oven when it starts to polymerize.
Use a biopsy punch to form holes of the desired diameter in the microfluidic chip surface.
Cut a piece of PDMS larger than required.
Remove excess PDMS from Petri dishes and place it onto the microfluidic chip.
Ensure no dust is present on both PDMS and chip surfaces.
Align holes on the microfluidic chip with those of PDMS.
Insert Teflon tubes through PDMS interconnector using a micropositioner.
Ensure tubes are 110% of microfluidic access hole diameter to prevent liquid leakage.
Connect tubes to liquid injection system if needed for user's application.
If necessary, add epoxy between the tube and PDMS for better adherence.
Cut the edge of the microtube straight using a new sharp blade.
Place the microtube in the access hole of the microfluidic chip carefully with the micropositioner.
Deposit epoxy on the access holes using an epoxy dispenser or manually place it.
Expose UV curable epoxy to a UV source for 3-10 minutes, depending on the quantity used.
Allow standard epoxy to cure at room temperature for 24 hours if the substrate is not exposed to high temperatures.
Rapidly solidify standard epoxy by exposing it to 100 °C if the microfluidic substrate needs to withstand high temperatures.
Solder surface-mount multipin electrical connectors to the PCB.
Clean the microfluidic chip's electrical pads with plasma oxygen if there is surface contamination; otherwise, clean with ethanol.
Cut conductive tape into small pieces matching the dimensions of the microfluidic chip's electrical pads using a sharp blade.
Place the cut conductive tape on the PCB electrical pads using forceps.
Align and place the microfluidic chip onto the PCB.
Attach an insulation layer (such as paper) to avoid short circuits before installing metal brackets depending on the location of PCB traces.
Use machine screws and nuts to attach the metal bracket.
Remove machine screws, nuts, and metal brackets for disassembly.
Gently separate the microfluidic chip from the PCB during disassembly.
Use ethanol to remove conductive tape adhesive from electrical pads prior to reassembly.
